subject: Post-call: Dedicated throughput & budget iteration for HelixData
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Suzanne Kim <suzanne.kim@helixdata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-27T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + a couple of capacity scenarios

Hi Suzanne — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the asks we want to make sure are captured before we put together a formal quote:  

- Estimated monthly token volume: 1.1–1.4B tokens (avg 1.2B). Peak week expected to be ~20% higher.  
- Typical prompt/response size: ~900–1,400 tokens per call (median ~1,000).
- Expected peak concurrency: ~45–70 concurrent requests during the 9am–12pm PDT window.
- Availability target: 99.9% SLA for production.
- Data control: traffic must remain within HelixData VPC (private deployment preferred) — we noted SOC 2 evidence request.

From a capacity standpoint you flagged low single-digit-second latency needs on 1k+ token responses and a desire to keep unit cost near $250–$400 per 1M tokens (budget band). You mentioned procurement may be able to sign a 12‑month reserved capacity commitment if the unit economics and throughput align.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll draft two reserved capacity scenarios (GPU mix, throughput estimates, and $/1M token guidance) for you and procurement.
2) Ben (cc'd) will follow up with a short benchmarking note on expected p95 latency for the two GPU choices with your median request size.
3) If either scenario looks reasonable, Marissa will pull together a term sheet + initial pricing and a draft MA for HelixData to review.

Attached: HelixData_Prod_Profile.xlsx — I captured the traffic profile you shared on the call. Please flag anything I got wrong.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
kar tik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Suzanne Kim <suzanne.kim@helixdata.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ernest Jensen <ernest.jensen@helixdata.com>
Date: 2027-05-27T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + a couple of capacity scenarios

Thanks Karthik — this matches our notes. A couple clarifications from my side:  

- The 1.2B/month is our conservative forecast; if the pilot drives adoption we could hit ~1.6B in month 4. Procurement is therefore most comfortable with a plan that has a clear scale path without huge step costs.
- For GPU preference: engineering prefers H100 family for latency, but they asked for a cost-comparable A100 variant as a lower-cost alternative.
- Our internal target is to hit $/1M tokens <= $300 for committed reserved capacity; $300–$400 is stretch depending on SLAs.

Procurement timeline: we have a budget window review on June 21; if we can get a term sheet + a clear cost model by June 10, we can slot Redwood for the Q3 reserved commit conversation.

Can you include approximate month-to-month unit cost curves (1–12 months) for each scenario? Ernest (procurement) is cc'd — he'll be the PO owner. Also, please include SOC2 and data residency summary in the next packet.

Appreciate it — Suzanne
Head of Product, HelixData
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Suzanne Kim <suzanne.kim@helixdata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-28T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + a couple of capacity scenarios

Suzanne — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a concise scenario packet (Redwood_HelixData_Scenarios.pdf) plus a short SOC2 summary. High-level, two capacity options that map to your volume/budget targets: 

Scenario Alpha (latency-first, reserved H100s)
- Reserved capacity: 8x H100 (private deployment/VPC)
- Estimated sustained aggregate throughput: ~3,200 tokens/sec across the pool; p95 latency for 1k–1.2k token responses: ~1.6–2.3s (single model, optimized kernels)
- Monthly token capacity comfortable band: 1.0–1.6B without degradation (auto-burst policy available)
- Unit economics (baseline): $220 per 1M tokens with a 12‑month commitment (volume tiering reduces to $185/1M at >1.5B/mo)

Scenario Beta (cost-first, reserved A100s)
- Reserved capacity: 12x A100 (private deployment/VPC)
- Estimated sustained aggregate throughput: ~2,600 tokens/sec; p95 latency for 1k–1.2k token responses: ~2.7–3.5s
- Monthly token capacity comfortable band: 0.9–1.4B (scale with extra lanes)
- Unit economics (baseline): $305 per 1M tokens with a 12‑month commitment (volume tiering reduces to $260/1M at >1.4B/mo)

Notes & assumptions:
- Baselines assume typical instruction-following model with KV cache enabled; the H100 number includes a conservative 10% uplift for real-world prompt variance.
- Pricing above factors in reserved GPU amortization, kernel licensing, and support. Quantized model variants (Q4/8-bit where applicable) can reduce effective $/1M by ~8–12% but may impact output quality for some prompts — Ben can share empirical evals.
- We can offer a short pilot (2–4 weeks) on hosted lanes that mirrors the production config for a hands-on perf/quality validation before signing. Pilot cost offsets apply to the first month of committed capacity if you convert.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Ben: pinged to attach a two-page perf note with p95 numbers and recommended model build.
2) Marissa: will draft a 1-page term sheet reflecting Scenario Alpha and Beta (including the volume-tier thresholds and PO timelines).
3) Karthik/Marissa: schedule a procurement sync week of June 7 to walk Ernest through the numbers and the MA draft.

If these two scenarios look directionally correct, we’ll convert the scenario PDF into a formal quote and finalize the MA draft.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

----

From: Suzanne Kim <suzanne.kim@helixdata.com>

Date: 2027-05-29T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + a couple of capacity scenarios

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly what I needed. Quick replies:  

- Scenario Alpha (8x H100) looks promising from engineering + cost perspective if the $220/1M baseline holds; the volume-tier to $185/1M at >1.5B/mo is compelling.
- Ernest will review the MA and the SOC2 doc; procurement would like the June 7 walkthrough.
- We’d like the pilot option to validate p95 on a 2-week window before formal commit. If the pilot matches the perf, we can sign a 12-month reserved PO within 10 business days after the procurement review.

Ernest — I’ve looped you in. Can you confirm whether HelixData needs an SOW or a PO-first flow? Also please request any additional legal redlines in advance so we can accelerate the June 21 budget review.

I’ll review the scenario PDF today and revert by EOD tomorrow with any redlines.

Thanks — Suzanne
Head of Product, HelixData
